text.p: Following are the main stories in Monday's Malaysian newspapers.
- The National Coalition won the expected landslide in Sarawak state elections but suffered a major casualty with the defeat of the state's deputy chief minister.
- State investment agency Permodalan Nasional Bhd will have to seek an estimated 12 billion ringgit worth of new investments in the next five years.
- The Indonesian government has agreed to the deportation of illegal Indonesian workers in Malaysia including those who have social and mental problems.
- The government has no plans to limit the number of cars going into Kuala Lumpur even after the light rail transit network is fully operational.
- The Malaysian government will not approve fresh applications for foreign maids from agencies until all illegals in the country are registered.
- The banking and finance sector will be asked to make greater efforts to meet the challenges of a more sophisticated economy and increased liberalisation.
